clue.text: Pipe obtained by a research establishment in the money

indicators.note: the research establishment sits inside the phrase for being rich, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: being in the money means being in cash, so the money is CASH
a lab, short for laboratory, is a research establishment

explanation.surface: Someone acquires a pipe from a wealthy research institute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the money' looks like a phrase about wealth, but here it is the container word itself: being in the money is being in cash.
explanation.definitionFit: A calabash is a large curved tobacco pipe made from a gourd, as smoked by Sherlock Holmes in films.

clue.text: Seek professional advice when cold and exhausted

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
all in is a colloquial phrase for worn out

explanation.surface: Someone who feels chilly and worn out decides to see a doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: To call in an expert is to summon them for professional help or advice.

clue.text: Brilliance and attraction surrounding good man

indicators.note: the attraction word goes around the abbreviation for a holy man

parts.note: a lure is an attraction or enticement
ST, for saint, is a good man

explanation.surface: A virtuous man is surrounded by sparkle and charm.
explanation.walkthrough: ST, short for saint, is the crossword convention for a good man.
explanation.definitionFit: Lustre is sheen or brilliance, a glossy shine.

clue.text: Brother is in France-in Brittany

definitions.note: the definition describes a place by its location, a city lying in Brittany

parts.note: est is the French word for is

explanation.surface: A sibling is in France, specifically the north-west region.
explanation.definitionFit: Brest is a port city at the western tip of Brittany in north-western France.

clue.text: Regal symbol demanding a form of respect

indicators.note: a form of the word means its letters are reshaped into another order

explanation.surface: A royal emblem that commands people's deference.
explanation.definitionFit: A sceptre is the ornamental staff carried by a monarch as an emblem of authority.

clue.text: Invent cosmetics

definitions.meaning: to make something up is to invent or concoct it
the general word for lipstick, powder and other cosmetics

explanation.definitionFit: The verb phrase means fabricate a story; the noun means face paint and powder.

clue.text: Rugby team with nothing but dark suits

parts.note: all, as in all talk, means nothing but
blacks are dark clothes, as in mourning dress

explanation.surface: A rugby side that dresses only in dark kit.
explanation.walkthrough: The All Blacks are the New Zealand national rugby team, known for their black strip.
explanation.definitionFit: The All Blacks are New Zealand's national rugby union team.

clue.text: One blend mixed is given a title

indicators.note: a mixed blend is shaken up, so its letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A single blend is stirred and awarded a name.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennobled means raised to the peerage, made a lord or lady.

clue.text: Prince tells stories to bishops

parts.note: to relate is to narrate or tell a story

explanation.surface: A royal recounts tales to senior clergymen.
explanation.definitionFit: Prelates are high-ranking churchmen such as bishops.

clue.text: Magazine for a phone-tapper

definitions.meaning: someone tapping a phone line is one who hears others' calls

explanation.walkthrough: The Listener was a BBC weekly magazine published from 1929 to 1991.
explanation.definitionFit: The Listener was a well-known British weekly magazine from the BBC, and an eavesdropper on phone calls hears them.

clue.text: Push under water with a soft thrust

parts.note: P, for piano, is the musical abbreviation for soft
a lunge is a sudden forward thrust, as in fencing

explanation.surface: Someone shoves another into a pool with a gentle push.
explanation.definitionFit: To plunge something is to immerse or dunk it suddenly below the surface.

clue.text: A mother and father to all

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal, especially livestock

explanation.surface: The universal parents, both mum and dad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mother and father' looks like one phrase, but the mother is DAM and the father is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis Adam is the first man, the ancestor of all humanity.

clue.text: Rat tried it out when bitten by fleas maybe

indicators.note: out signals that the letters are put out of their usual order and rearranged

parts.note: the setter's fodder, which as printed carries one T more than the answer needs

explanation.surface: A rodent experiments, then gets irritated when fleas bite it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' is the anagram signal. As printed, RATTRIEDIT has ten letters with three Ts, one more than the nine-letter answer, so the fodder is taken as RATTRIEDI.
explanation.definitionFit: Flea bites cause itching and annoyance, so someone so bitten is plausibly vexed, as the 'maybe' concedes.

clue.text: Light Infantry standing beside a North African state

parts.note: LI is the standard military abbreviation for Light Infantry
by means next to or beside

explanation.surface: A regiment of soldiers is stationed next to a country in North Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Libya is a country on the Mediterranean coast of North Africa, between Egypt and Tunisia.

clue.text: Survey property for burglary action in court

definitions.meaning: to ... a joint is slang for checking a building over before robbing it
a lawsuit or trial is a legal ...

explanation.definitionFit: Thieves' slang for reconnoitring a target, and the ordinary word for a lawsuit.

clue.text: Understand how to make an arrest

definitions.meaning: to seize and take someone into custody

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both grasp mentally and seize a suspect.

clue.text: In the Middle East teach to make weapon

indicators.note: the scrambled teaching word goes within the abbreviation for the region

parts.note: ME is the usual abbreviation for the Middle East

indicators.note: the letters are used to make something new, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone in the Middle East is taught to fashion a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to make' is the anagram signal, rearranging the five letters of 'teach'; 'In' then places them within ME.
explanation.definitionFit: A machete is a broad heavy knife used as a tool or as a weapon.

clue.text: Scare created by proprietorial claim in ten

indicators.note: the claim to ownership is placed inside the marsh word

parts.note: a fen is a low marshy area, as in East Anglia
a right is a legal claim to property

explanation.surface: Someone is alarmed by a claim of ownership over marshland.
explanation.walkthrough: The page reads 'ten', an OCR or print slip for 'fen', a marsh, which the wordplay needs; nothing in 'ten' gives the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To frighten someone is to scare or alarm them.

clue.text: Marlborough's success when he was in nimble form

indicators.note: the letters are put into a new form, rearranged

explanation.surface: The Duke's victory came while he was in agile shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form' is the anagram signal on HE and NIMBLE. The Duke of Marlborough won the Battle of Blenheim in 1704.
explanation.definitionFit: The Battle of Blenheim in 1704 was the Duke of Marlborough's great victory over the French.

clue.text: King to pass and return to former state

parts.note: R, for Rex, is the abbreviation for king
time is said to elapse when it passes

explanation.surface: A monarch lets time go by and things slip back to how they were.
explanation.definitionFit: To relapse is to fall back into an earlier condition, especially illness or bad habits.

clue.text: A serious test for the PM?

definitions.text: A serious test for the PM?

parts.words: A serious test for the PM?
parts.note: a hard test; cryptically, what PM is to a former morning, since after noon the time is no longer morning

explanation.walkthrough: PM follows AM, so the afternoon is literally ex-AM: once morning.
explanation.definitionFit: An exam is a formal test, and split it reads as former morning, which afternoon is.

clue.text: Desire disorderly slut

indicators.note: something disorderly is out of order, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An insult about an untidy woman paired with craving.
explanation.definitionFit: Lust is strong desire, especially sexual craving.

clue.text: Hawaiian welcome certain to suggest holidaying

parts.note: a lei is the garland of flowers given to greet visitors in Hawaii
sure means certain

explanation.surface: A garland greeting in Hawaii is bound to put you in a vacation mood.
explanation.definitionFit: Leisure is free time away from work, the state of being on holiday.

clue.text: Goat found in Penang or Arabia

indicators.note: the letters are found inside the run of words that follow

explanation.surface: A goat discovered in Malaysia or the Middle East.
explanation.definitionFit: The Angora is a breed of goat whose long hair gives mohair.

clue.text: Country sounds as if it may reduce friction

indicators.note: signals that the word heard is spelt differently from the one entered

parts.note: grease is a lubricant that reduces friction

explanation.surface: A nation whose name evokes a lubricant.
explanation.definitionFit: Greece is a country in south-eastern Europe.

clue.text: Particular type of variegated green

indicators.note: variegated means multicoloured and mixed, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A gardener describes a special kind of multicoloured green foliage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variegated' looks like a plant description but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A genre is a category or kind, especially of art or writing.

clue.text: A Far Eastern country gets wrought iron from part of Eurasian land mass

parts.note: Siam is the old name of Thailand

indicators.note: wrought means worked or shaped, so the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: An Asian nation obtains worked metal from a region of the great continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrought iron' reads as the metal, but 'wrought' rearranges IRON into MINOR. SIAM is the former name of Thailand.
explanation.definitionFit: Asia Minor is the peninsula of Anatolia, the westernmost part of Asia, which joins Europe to form Eurasia.

clue.text: Excessively masculine description of zero air-speed

parts.note: Mach is the unit giving air speed relative to the speed of sound
O looks like zero

explanation.surface: Something overly manly is described as having no speed through the air.
explanation.walkthrough: Mach 0 means not moving at all through the air; 'description of' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: Macho means aggressively or exaggeratedly manly.

clue.text: Sheets written out for dissertations

indicators.note: writing the letters out again in another order rearranges them

explanation.surface: Students write pages for their long essays.
explanation.definitionFit: A thesis is a long academic essay, so the plural means dissertations.

clue.text: Just a nip for a chap who can nip it

definitions.meaning: a nip is a small drink, a swift tipple taken in a hurry

definitions.text: a chap who can nip it
definitions.meaning: someone nimble who can nip about is a fast person

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a swift drink, and read literally also describes a speedy person who can dash.

clue.text: Damson puree for people of no fixed abode

indicators.note: fruit made into a puree is mashed up, so the letters are mashed

explanation.surface: Wandering folk are served a mashed plum dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'puree' sounds culinary, but it is the anagram signal; a damson is a small plum.
explanation.definitionFit: Nomads are wanderers who move from place to place with no permanent home.

clue.text: Set off for school in time

indicators.note: the school sits within the word for time, so one goes inside the other

parts.note: a date is a particular time
Eton is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: A pupil leaves for school on schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set off' looks like departing, but it means explode. ETON is the famous English boarding school.
explanation.definitionFit: To detonate a bomb is to set it off, making it explode.
